title: Lookahead Sample Reward Guidance for Test-Time Scaling of Diffusion Models
claim: Compute future-reward guidance from a few cheap lookahead samples, then use their reward-weighted directions to steer sampling toward high-reward regions.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, flag icons mark reward, inset zooms on guidance vector
description: Two side-by-side panels, each showing a trajectory from a noise blob p(x_T) on the left toward a data distribution on the right. A legend at top left uses red, orange and pink flags for high, mid and low reward. Panel (a), Phase 1, shows three gray trajectories of lookahead samples ending in blue density clouds. Each endpoint carries a flag and a cow-image thumbnail with a colored border, which shows the reward annotation. Panel (b), Phase 2, shows a black particle trajectory with a red gradient arrow and a zoomed inset. The inset shows red, green and blue dotted vectors, which attract the particle to the high-reward sample and repel it from the low-reward ones. An orange reward-tilted density with a star-marked sample x0 appears at the right. Red math at top gives the guidance sum. Captions under each panel name the phases. The eye goes first to the cow images and flags.
caption: Overview of the proposed sampling framework from prompt $\rvc$. (a) To obtain marginal samples, we generate lookahead samples using a few-step solver and annotate them with a reward function. (b) To generate samples from the target reward-tilted distribution, LiDAR guides particles $\rvx_t$ toward high-reward lookahead sample $\hat{\rvx}_0^{1}$ and repels low-reward lookahead samples $\hat{\rvx}_0^{2}, \hat{\rvx}_0^{3}$. The guiding weight $w_i^r - w_i$ provided by each lookahead sample $\hat{\rvx}_0^{i}$ is proportional to its reward annotation value; see [ref] for the definition.
abstract: Diffusion models have demonstrated strong generative performance; however, generated samples often fail to fully align with human intent. This paper studies an efficient test-time scaling method for sampling from regions with higher human-aligned reward values. Existing methods for computing the expected future reward (EFR) face important limitations: backward rollout incurs prohibitively high sampling costs, while Tweedie-based approaches, including Sequential Monte Carlo and gradient guidance, suffer from bias and inherent sampling issues. We show that the EFR at any $\mathbf{x}_t$ can be computed using only marginal samples from a pre-trained diffusion model, enabling closed-form reward guidance without neural backpropagation. To further improve efficiency, we introduce a few-step lookahead sampling and an accurate solver that guides particles toward high-reward lookahead samples. We refer to this sampling scheme as LiDAR sampling. LiDAR achieves the same GenEval performance as the latest gradient guidance method for SDXL with a 9.5x speedup. We release the code at https://github.com/aailab-kaist/Diffusion-LiDAR-Sampling.
